versions.label: 1976 map
versions.long: Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1976, as amended
sources: Numbers, names, Lok Sabha seats: ECI, Statistical Report on the General Elections 2004, Vol. III (Assembly segments)
Reservations: the pre-2008 map file (T3); totals checked against the 2008 Order, Schedule II
AC shapes: ECI via DataMeet (india-geodata eci-statewise), placed on the map by a fitted transform; median error 0.14 km
PC shapes: merged from the AC shapes
notes: Seat numbers, names and Lok Sabha seats are those in force before 2008, as ECI's report on the 2004 Lok Sabha election lists them. Assembly reservations come from the pre-2008 map file; their totals equal the 2008 Order's Schedule II.

The pre-2008 map was placed on the ground by a fitted transform (median distance from the state's 2008 outline 0.14 km), then fitted to the state's outer boundary, which did not change in 2008; gaps along the edge went to the neighbouring seat.
This is the map after the 2000 reorganisation of states: the 1976 Order's seats as renumbered for the new state.

caution.reason: Small seat (under 60 km²): a placing error of a few hundred metres is a large share of it, so a place near its edge may belong to the neighbouring seat. City seats are the least reliable (in Bombay the source map had to be redrawn).

versions.label: 2008 map
versions.long: Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 2008
sources: Numbers, names, reservations, Lok Sabha seats: ECI, Statistical Report on the General Elections 2009 (Assembly segments); 3 reservation(s) taken from the 2008 Order, where the report differs
AC shapes: DataMeet India_AC (T3); Indore-1 to Indore-5 drawn from ECI polling-station locations (modelled), since DataMeet has one polygon for the city; PCs merged from them with ECI's lists

caution.reason: Indore city seat, drawn from ECI polling-station locations (2017): DataMeet's map has one polygon for the whole city, and the 2008 Order's ward lists cannot be placed (no map of the 2001 wards). Each place goes to the seat of its nearest polling station, inside DataMeet's city block; the lines are approximate.
